claim: \emph{Margin and engineering freedom.} A quantitative model establishes a response-time tolerance of 200 ms. Alignment measures two implementations against that bound: A has 80 ms of margin, while B has 5 ms. Both conform, but their remaining headroom differs. The measurements can guide an agent’s exploration of implementation alternatives and inform the engineer’s subsequent design and governance decisions. Measured margin is evidence about available freedom, not a guarantee.

alt: Modeling defines a response-time obligation of at most 200 milliseconds. A schematic acceptable-region axis locates implementation A at 120 milliseconds with 80 milliseconds of margin and B at 195 milliseconds with 5 milliseconds of margin. Alignment measures the behavior; agents can explore alternatives within headroom and engineers reassess design or controls as margin shrinks. A feedback arrow returns measured evidence to Modeling. Measured margin is evidence, not a guarantee.
